Results.ReviewText: This charcoal grill is the updated equivalent of the Weber grill we used for over 30 years.  We had an issue with the lid vent on the new one.   That was a factory installed vent so Weber sent us a new lid!  All is well now.    We look forward to grilling for many years on this new grill.
Results.Title: Best charcoal grill!!

Results.ReviewText:
This 22" Weber Kettle Grill replaced a knock off 18" kettle grill.  The copy-cat 18" grill failed after just one year.  The Weber has a better fit and finish and the taste is superior to the knock of grill.  The Weber 22" was only a few dollars more than the shoddy knock-off grill. 

This Weber is now fitted with a cast iron cooking grate and charcoal pans which improves the performance with regards to temperature control and clean up.  Two (2) recommended add-ons, in my opinion.

The only negative is that it takes up more room than I expected.
Results.Title: 22" Weber Kettle Grill - plain jane original

Results.ReviewText: The grill works great I am still learning how to adjust the air vents for my desired results.  Since I like to grill dinner food and multi- task I  should have splurged for the more expensive model with the hinged lid and hinged grate to allow quicker and easier adjustments.
Results.Title: Extra Features

Results.ReviewText: Hard to go wrong with this design - had one years ago and happy to be re-united - food always seems perfectly cooked, easy to regulate heat, easy to tote from back to front yard for neighborhood cookouts.

Results.ReviewText:
It's too expensive for what you get.  I bought two of these and one of them the lid doesn't fit right.  It also came with a chip in the lid pre-installed, so there's that. 

It cooks.  As it should.  But it wasn't anything noteworthy.  Average quality, it does what it's supposed to.  

If I were giving it a grade, it'd be a C.

Weber has started charging more and giving less with these.  Little things you normally wouldn't notice, like the thickness of the metal, overall.  Or the quality of components compared to older models. 

It is what is.  3 Stars.
Results.Title: Quality for Price isn't Great.

 Maybe in the past you built quality grills that is not the case any longer.

Results.ReviewText: Weber is not standing behind the 10 year guarantee anymore. Results.ReviewText:
The old Weber that my parents bought in the mid 70s. Judging by the lid vent, and bowl vent tabs, I'd call it a 1975. It has been in use every summer up until this year (2024). One of the leg sockets detached from the bowl and due to rust, will probably not be able to be repaired. I'm going to try though.
I just bought a new Original Kettle 22 inch. Build quality seems comparable to the one my parents bought, so I'm assuming another 50 years of service from this one. I'll definitely be dead by the.
Results.Title: Just retiring the old Kettle from 1975

Results.ReviewText: Only thing we would change is to have a pan underneath to catch the ashes.

Results.ReviewText: About a year ago my gas grill rusted out so all I had left was my Weber kettle.  Never replaced my gas grill, just started only using charcoal.  Have never looked back.  All food so much better and the Weber Kettle remains the best tool to control heat and smoke with charcoal.  I've cooked the Thanksgiving Turkey on my Kettle at least 4 times.   I drove my kettle into the ground, finally it died and I ordered another.
Results.Title: Like an old friend

Results.ReviewText: I switched back to charcoal from gas for the flavor so I can add wood chips directly on the coals.  I’ve been messing around with the different positions in the Weber owner manual.  I can get the required 2hrs of smoke to ribs and then still have enough heat to put the ribs in the aluminum pan with a little apple cider vinegar covered to give it that little bit of extra flavor and to tenderize them.  To finish them off I char them with BBQ sauce and serve.  Burgers and ribeyes I just use hickory or apple/cherry chips.  For straight burgers I use mesquite chips because of the strong flavor.  I haven’t done a shoulder yet so I’ll see how it does the shoulder later as it takes a good 6-8 hours to get it cooked to the right temperature full making pulled pork.
Results.Title: Weber quality as always.

Results.ReviewText: There is nothing better than grilling with a charcoal grill. Need to add a Weber original charcoal grill to your grilling collection!
Results.Title: Weber Original Charcoal Grill

Results.ReviewText: After years of purchasing nice expensive grilles, inly to have them quicky die, we decided to go back to basics and get a lower cost charcoal grille. This is about as simple as you can get, nothing to break/rust/run out of gas/etc. The ash pan could be better - deeper and easier to remove. Need to plan meals a bit better too - no more going out and flipping a switch. But its good. Looking forward to a long life.
Results.Title: Back to Basics

Results.ReviewText: I love my Weber Grill, I have had Weber's throughout my life and they always serve me very well, even with the advent of Pellet grills, they always taste so much better than any gas grill I have ever owned, I always come back to the best there is out there! The Weber Grill can't be beat.

Photos.Caption: Sits like this when I put the lid on instead of immediately flush

Results.ReviewText:
I love Weber products, and love their kettle grills. I just had a bad experience with my new 22 inch kettle. It came damaged on the box. Lid has a dent on the side and make it not sit flush on top of the grill. It’s lopsided now due to the dent. The grill itself also seems to have been pressed on or squeezed between something during transit because it is not a circle, it came more oval than anything else. I had to manipulate it to be as circular as possible. It was too much to return it online since I had a cookout that same day.
But this is just one bad experience and my last Weber grill was great! Just want that to be clear.
Results.Title: Great grills, bad experience
